One timeline, different places

Apple Photos can add one known place. LensPin matches the whole trip.

Manual adjustment is perfect when you know the place. A travel timeline is different: every camera photo may belong somewhere else along the route.

Apple Photos

A review-first workflow

From missing location to a result you can inspect.

  1. Choose the date range, camera, and evidenceUse a timestamped GPX track, geotagged iPhone photos, or both. LensPin only considers camera photos that do not already have a location.
  2. Check the suggested locationsSee the map point, capture time, nearby evidence, source agreement, and why a photo is marked reliable, needs review, or has no suggestion.
  3. Confirm what gets savedHigh-confidence suggestions are selected by default. You stay in control, and LensPin checks again before writing each location.

Evidence, not a black box

Know why a photo landed there.

A score helps sort suggestions; it is not a probability and never means the original GPS was recovered. Track gaps, distant anchors, and source conflicts stay visible.

Save safely

Nothing changes until you confirm.

LensPin is designed around the awkward parts of a real Photos library: existing locations, iCloud downloads, unsupported edits, and incomplete evidence.

✓

Existing locations stay protected

Only photos without a location enter the matching flow. LensPin checks again before writing and skips a photo if a location appeared meanwhile.

!

No suggestion is a valid result

If a track is broken or location evidence is too far from the capture time, LensPin shows the reason instead of guessing.

⌁

Photos and GPX stay on the device

Matching is local. Automatic time-zone lookup may send a small number of coordinates to Apple’s geocoding service; the photos and GPX file are not uploaded.

Questions before you start

LensPin FAQ

Do I need a GPX file?

No. LensPin can use geotagged iPhone photos taken around the same time. A GPX track usually gives denser evidence, and you can use both sources together.

Does LensPin import photos from my camera?

No. Import them with Apple Photos, a compatible card reader, or your camera maker’s workflow first. LensPin works with camera photos already in Apple Photos.

What if my camera clock was wrong?

You can apply a camera clock offset for matching. It changes the time LensPin compares against the evidence; it does not change the photo’s capture time.

Does it change the original photo?

Saving a Photos-library location does not replace the original file. An optional EXIF GPS edit uses Apple Photos’ non-destructive current edit version, so the original remains recoverable.

What happens when LensPin is not confident?

The photo moves to Review or No Suggestion with an explanation. Low-confidence or conflicting results are not selected as safe defaults.

Does it work with iCloud Photos?

Yes, but originals stored only in iCloud may need to download before scanning or optional EXIF editing can finish. Learn more in the iCloud Photos guide.
